world_frame_note: env: per-env origin on the floor plan, z up; state, action, object and camera poses all use it. Each env is an independent copy of the scene; the episode's T_world_env (pure translation env_origin_world_m, no rotation) maps it to the simulation world

state_indices.note: single-arm Franka: the one arm is duplicated into both slots, so dual-arm sums computed from them (e.g. export_features.py total_ee_path_length = left + right) are 2x the true single-arm value; left_* and right_* displacement / gripper range are identical

action_semantics_detail: next_sample_single_arm_absolute_cartesian_pose_and_gripper_target; the last frame's action is the pose / gripper target of the terminal frame, which is not itself recorded

feature_units.observation.contact_force: N, world z up; net contact force on each finger and on the plug (all partners)
feature_units.observation.keypoint_error: m (mean distance between the plug keypoints and their seated positions)
feature_units.policy_action: dimensionless in [-1, 1]: the insertion policy's action (position / rotation increments in the socket frame, scaled by the controller thresholds); zero outside the insert phase
feature_units.phase_index: index into phases.names (0 approach, 1 grasp, 2 lift, 3 carry, 4 insert, 5 release, 6 return)

gripper_definition: state gripper_open = mean of the two finger joints / 0.04 m (0 closed, 1 fully open); action gripper = the commanded finger opening as the same fraction at the next frame: 1 open while approaching and releasing, the training opening (gripper_open_width / 0.04) while pre-closing, 0 closed from the close on through the insertion

depth_format.container: roboassemblybench_chunked_depth_v1: file header struct '<8sI' = magic b'RABDU16\0' + version 1; then per frame a chunk header struct '<III' = (frame_index, uncompressed_size, compressed_size) followed by compressed_size bytes of one zstd frame
depth_format.chunks[].offset: byte offset of the frame's 12-byte chunk header (the zstd frame starts at offset + 12)
depth_format.filter: bitplane16_le: the zstd payload holds 16 bit planes (bit 0 first) of the frame's row-major uint16 samples, each plane packed with numpy packbits(bitorder='little'); it is NOT the bitshuffle library's blocked layout
depth_format.values: uint16 millimetres, 0 = invalid; depth = distance to the image plane (z in the camera optical frame)
depth_format.reader: decode: zstd-decompress, reshape to (16, ceil(N / 8)) bytes, unpackbits(bitorder='little')[:N] per plane, value |= bit << plane

depth_note: depth omitted in this sample export (--no-depth); the full dataset carries the depth sidecar described in depth_format
success_definition: pick, carry and insertion reach the target (mean keypoint error < 0.003 m), the gripper opens, the arm returns to the fixed home pose, and the mean keypoint error is still < 0.003 m at the last frame; or, for episodes with success_rule = deeper_ok in episodes.jsonl, the deeper_ok rule in success_rules; only successful episodes are kept

success_rules.keypoint: pick, carry and insertion reach the target (mean keypoint error < 0.003 m), the gripper opens, the arm returns to the fixed home pose, and the mean keypoint error is still < 0.003 m at the last frame

deeper_ok.rule: for assemblies whose AutoMate goal pose has no physical stop (e.g. a sleeve on a post, a hole deeper than the goal): the target is reached (mean keypoint error < strict threshold) before the release, and at the last frame the plug base is at most 0.003 m out of the goal along the socket axis (any depth further in), at most 0.003 m off laterally and tilted at most 5.0 deg; the mean keypoint error at the last frame can then exceed the strict threshold

target_reached_definition: a frame with mean keypoint error < 0.003 m (plug at its seated pose)

grasp_raise.note: episodes.jsonl grasp_raise_m: the nominal AutoMate grasp (plug_grasps.json) moved back by this distance along the fingertip approach axis, i.e. the fingertips grasp the plug that much higher, in the pick and in the policy's training reset; used on tasks whose original grasp is at or below the table surface

attachment_assist.kind: none: the plug is held by finger friction only (no attachment, welding or pose writes); after the insertion the gripper opens

description.approach: home pose -> 8 cm above the policy grasp on the plug standing on the table -> down to the grasp pose, gripper fully open
description.grasp: fingers to the training opening, then closed until they stop
description.carry: up to the cruise height, over the socket, down to the policy start pose (plug 10 mm above the entrance, measured in-hand transform)
description.insert: the insertion policy until the mean keypoint error is < strict_thresh
description.return: 8 cm up, back to the home pose, still there for 0.5 s

control.controller: task-space impedance on the fingertip in every phase; insert: target = fingertip + scaled policy action (EMA-smoothed), action in the socket frame (D16); scripted phases: clipped targets toward waypoints
control.joint_commands: not recorded (the controller outputs joint torques); measured joint states are in joint_state

orientation.roll_pitch: policy-controlled within 10.0 deg of upright (per-task unlock)

pick_contact_check.rule: during approach and grasp, the upward (world +z) net contact force on the two fingers, summed, must stay <= the limit: a gripper pushed onto the table to reach the grasp fails the episode (finger_pressed_table, not kept); the episode's maximum is in metrics.pick.finger_up_contact_force_max_n

descend_landing.rule: descent onto the plug: each control step moves at most land_gain x the remaining error (no jump to the goal), so the arm slows down as it arrives

scripted_waypoints.rule: approach / grasp / lift / carry run in lock step over the envs; an env outside the waypoint tolerance is stalled when over the window its error in motion steps (d / max_lin + ang / max_ang) dropped by less than stall_far_rate x window while still moving, or its position and angle errors both dropped by less than stall_min_progress near the waypoint; a stalled env is no longer waited for; stalled farther than stall_fail from the waypoint = the pick fails (servo_stalled, not kept)

scripted_waypoints_note: episodes.jsonl descend_landing: the soft-landing descent (each control step moves at most land_gain x the remaining error, no jump to the goal) used by the episode, null for episodes collected before it was introduced

metric_definitions.kp_final_m: the larger of the mean keypoint error at the last recorded frame and at the terminal (unrecorded) state
metric_definitions.seat_final: plug base relative to its goal in the socket frame at the last frame: axial_m (+ = out), lateral_m, tilt_deg
metric_definitions.finger_up_contact_force_max_n: maximum upward (world +z) net contact force on the two fingers, summed, during approach and grasp

joint_commands: not recorded (the controller outputs joint torques); measured joint states are observation.joint_*

visual_randomization.applied: once per round, right after the env reset and before the first recorded frame; constant within an episode
visual_randomization.order_note: the four parts write disjoint scene elements (listed under each part), so another order gives the same scene
visual_randomization.seeding: visual_seeds[part] = [run_seed, stream, round, env]; stream 1 lighting, 2 distractors, 3 surface_textures, 4 scene_props

elements: /World/Light (dome light, shared by all envs of a round)

distractors.types: Distractor_<k>: box for even k, cylinder for odd k (category primitive_box / primitive_cylinder)
distractors.physics: visual only (no collision, no rigid body)
distractors.placement: standing on the table top; x U(0.3, 0.95) m, y U(-0.45, 0.45) m (env frame); >= 0.10 m from the socket and from the plug, >= 0.08 m from the socket-plug segment and from the front camera's lines of sight to both; up to 50 tries, otherwise that distractor is hidden (the recorded list holds the visible ones)

type_distribution.v1_20261004: deterministic by slot: Distractor_k is a box for even k and a cylinder for odd k, so with n visible distractors there are ceil(n/2) boxes and floor(n/2) cylinders, listed box first; over n = 0..4 boxes : cylinders = 60 : 40, and a single distractor is always a box (episodes collected 2026-10-04..10-10)
type_distribution.v2_20261010: each distractor slot independently a box or a cylinder with probability 1/2 each (every slot is an Xform holding one box and one cylinder, the other one made invisible); n = U{0..4} as in v1 (episodes collected from 2026-10-10 15:57 CST; first 1,808 distractors: 900 boxes, 908 cylinders)

elements: floor material /World/Looks/CollectFloor on the ground plane (shared by all envs of a round)

floor.texture: one of 3 upstream Fabrica textures: floor/T_Metal_Glossy_A_Albedo.png, floor/T_Plastic_Gray_A_Albedo.png, floor/t_corrugatedboxes_b01_tile02_albedo.png

table.choice: per env 50 / 50: plain colour or texture
table.plain_colour: one of the 6 upstream Fabrica table_surface palette colours [[0.14,0.14,0.14],[0.28,0.31,0.32],[0.22,0.30,0.25],[0.33,0.24,0.25],[0.25,0.27,0.36],[0.40,0.36,0.25]] (a 1x1 white texture tinted by it, tiling 1)
table.texture: one of 4 upstream Fabrica textures: table/T_Wood_Laminate_Gray_A_Albedo.png, table/T_Wood_Pressed_A1_Albedo.png, table/T_MetalPainted_White_Glossy_A_Albedo.png, table/T_Plastic_Gray_A_Albedo.png; tiling U(1, 3)
table.appearance_probabilities: plain colour 0.5 (each of the 6 palette colours 1/12) / texture 0.5 (each of the 4 textures 1/8)

surface_textures.asset_registry: data/visual_assets/fabrica_textures/manifest.json (file -> upstream path, sha256); every episode records the file and its sha256

scene_props.assets: 16 Isaac 5.1 assets: Simple_Warehouse props SM_BarelPlastic_A_01, SM_BarelPlastic_C_01, SM_CardBoxA_01, SM_CardBoxA_02, SM_CardBoxB_01, SM_CardBoxC_01, SM_CratePlastic_A_04, SM_FuseBox_01, SM_PaletteA_01, SM_PaletteA_02, SM_PushcartA_02, SM_WallA_6M, SM_WallWire_08, S_TrafficCone, Props/Forklift/forklift, Props/KLT_Bin/small_KLT_visual
scene_props.placement: on the ground (z -0.4 m), 2-6 m from the front camera inside its horizontal field of view, yaw U(0, 360); oriented footprints clear the env keep-out box (arm, table, both cameras) and each other; never inside another env's front view

selection.v1_20261004: each env and round: n = U{3..6}, the 16 assets in a uniformly random order, placed in that order until n fit; every asset has about the same frequency, so a category's frequency is proportional to its number of assets (cardboard_box 4 assets, barrel 2, pallet 2, the other 8 categories 1 each: cardboard boxes appear about 4x as often as a traffic cone or the forklift) (episodes collected 2026-10-04..10-10)
selection.v2_20261010: each env and round: n = U{3..6}; the order of the 16 assets is built by repeatedly drawing a category uniformly among the categories that still have assets left, then one of its remaining assets uniformly; props are placed in that order until n fit (a prop that does not fit is skipped, a second pass retries the skipped ones). A category with several assets (cardboard_box 4, barrel 2, pallet 2) can recur within an episode and stays in the draw after the one-asset categories are used, so it is realised somewhat more often (first 4,150 props: cardboard_box 477, pallet 428, barrel 419, the other 8 categories 331-373) (episodes collected from 2026-10-10 15:57 CST)

not_randomized.ground_plane: Isaac Lab GroundPlaneCfg default_environment.usd at z -0.4 m (its material is the floor texture above)
not_randomized.cameras: fixed: D435 front (env frame) and D405 wrist (on panda_hand); intrinsics and mounts constant

visual_randomization.actual_values: per episode in metadata environment (lights, table, ground, distractors, scene_props) and domain_randomization.params; LeRobot export: meta/diversity/environments.jsonl

exposure_filter.rule: an episode is rejected (not kept) when, in the first recorded frame of the front camera (arm at the home pose), the table region (rows 300-480, cols 120-520 of the 640 x 480 image, luma of the decoded video) has a median >= 239 (table rendered close to white) or >= 3 % of its pixels >= 250 (a clipped light spot)
exposure_filter.why: the renderer has no auto exposure; bright dome light combined with a strong, close key light and a pale table colour or texture washes the table out (first scan 2026-10-10: 2,769 of 25,840 collected episodes, 10.7 %; 4-16 % per task); threshold set from a user review of 16 first frames on 2026-10-10
exposure_filter.effect_on_distributions: the realised lighting / table-look combinations exclude the brightest ones: the parameter ranges in parts.lighting and parts.surface_textures are the sampling ranges before this filter; per-episode actual values are in environments.jsonl
exposure_filter.applies_to: every episode of the dataset (v1_20261004 and v2_20261010)

asset_registry.note: texture ids are paths relative to the upstream Fabrica texture set; sha256 per episode in environments.jsonl

environment_field_mapping.background_texture: the floor (ground plane) texture of the episode
environment_field_mapping.table_texture: the table texture file, or the Fabrica palette colour of a plain table
environment_field_mapping.clutter: visual-only distractors on the table; background warehouse props are scene content (environments.jsonl scene_props)

coordinate_note: T_world_camera maps camera optical (OpenCV) coordinates to the episode's env frame; T_world_env in episodes.jsonl maps the env frame to the simulation world (pure translation)
frame_rate_provenance: 30 Hz recording (physics 120 Hz, every 4 steps); timestamp = frame_index / fps
